title: CI continuous performance sentinel harness with distribution-aware baselining
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem:
Current CI perf gates are brittle for low-latency bursty workloads: single-point p95 comparisons and fixed token/sec thresholds create many false-positives when PRs touch kernel selection, batching heuristics, or seed-dependent workload mixes. We need a CI sentinel that understands distribution shape, context-conditioned baselines, and signals uncertainty so engineers get actionable, low-noise alerts instead of noisy gating failures.

Proposal summary:
Build a "sentinel" harness that runs as part of PR CI and nightly baselining. Key ideas:
- Dual baselines: (1) rolling production shadow baseline (last 7 days) and (2) stable reference baseline for the release branch. Use ensemble scoring to detect drift against either baseline.
- Distribution-aware checks: evaluate p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec jointly via conditional quantile mapping rather than single-threshold comparisons.
- Statistical engine: combine robust statistics (MAD, trimmed means), control-chart style EWMA for small samples, and a Bayesian change-probability output to quantify regression confidence.
- Adaptive sample sizing: if variance is high, increase synthetic sample size (longer runs or microburst stitching) to reduce noise before gating.
- Synthetic microburst stitching: synthesize short burst workloads by concatenating representative traces to exercise kernel scheduling and cache effects deterministically.
- Traffic shadowing mode: when possible, run candidate builds in shadow against production-like traffic replay for higher-fidelity signals.
- CI actionability: for PRs with medium confidence regressions, create a lightweight inline report with run artifacts (trace, flamegraph, kernel selector histogram) and recommended next steps (re-run with larger sample, file for perf review, or revert). High confidence regressions should block merge per gating policy.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- We accept slightly longer CI perf checks (typical +30-90s) in exchange for dramatically lower false positive rate; gating remains fast for clear pass/fail cases.
- Ensemble baselines increase storage and compute cost; we cap full replays to nightly jobs and use lightweight shadow sampling on PRs.
- Bayesian alarms give probability rather than binary labels, enabling manual override and follow-up investigations.

Acceptance criteria:
- The sentinel runs on every PR touching runtime code paths or performance-critical configuration files.
- False-positive rate (blocked PRs that pass manual perf review) reduced by >=70% compared to current p95-only gate on our historical sample (analyze last 90 days of CI failures).
- At least 90% of high-confidence regressions correlate with downstream nightly baseline alarms or production incidents in a 30-day post-detection window (precision target).
- Generated CI report links to: regression dashboard, GitHub PR, perf trace bundle, and suggested remediation checklist.
- Sentinel integrates with current CI orchestration (buildkite) and uploads artifacts to S3/perf-buckets under standardized path.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Build baseline store and retrieval API (rolling and stable baselines). Add metadata: context window, sequence length distribution, model variant, kernel profile.
2) Implement microburst synthetic workload generator and deterministic trace stitching harness.
3) Statistical engine: implement combined MAD+EWMA+Bayesian module and expose simple pass/fail/confidence outputs.
4) CI integration: PR hook step (fast shadow sample) + nightly full replay job.
5) Report renderer: HTML/JSON perf report for PRs with links to flamegraphs and kernel selection histograms.
6) Oncall runbook and rollback policies for blocked changes.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for statistical engine and false-positive/false-negative simulations using historic CI traces.
- End-to-end smoke: run sentinel on a curated set of 40 prior PRs (mix of known regressions and safe changes) and validate detection performance.
- Canary the PR-step on 'team-runtime' repo for two weeks before making it required for merges.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Start as optional PR check (status context only) for 2 weeks and surface reports to reviewers.
- After validation, flip to required for runtime repo with soft-blocks (warning period) then hard-block.
- Monitor gate metrics in Console: gate TTTR (time-to-result), false-positive rate, blocked PR count, and compute cost.

Notes and follow-ups:
- This ticket focuses on the sentinel logic and CI hook. Subsequent tickets will: add tight integration with the rollout service for automatic fallback, add per-customer baseline slicing, and expose guardrail tuning in the Console.
- Coordinate with SDK and infra teams to standardize trace formats.
